column1: # The SLOW band's tolerated-red set — ENUMERATED, so it is checkable.
# your-org/nexus-code#737: a band that is both non-blocking AND carries a
# known-red set is the configuration in which a genuine new red is
# indistinguishable from the accepted ones. #559 named the tolerated set but
# never wrote it down, and a tolerated-red list that is cultural cannot be
# checked. This file is that list as data; monitor/slow-band-drift.sh is what
# checks it, in BOTH directions:
#   a red NOT listed here          -> NEW-RED, the job fails. This is the whole
#                                     point: a new regression is loud again.
#   a listed test that now PASSES  -> STALE-TOLERATION, the job fails. Without
#                                     this direction the list only ever grows
#                                     and becomes a permanent excuse; a red that
#                                     was fixed must cost someone one deletion.
# THE SELF-CLEANING PROPERTY ABOVE IS INHERITED, NOT INTRINSIC. STALE-TOLERATION
# only ever fires on a run that actually HAPPENS. It is the per-PR/per-push
# triggers in .github/workflows/tests-slow-integration.yml that make those runs
# happen; the checker cannot notice that nobody is calling it. Revert that band
# to schedule-only, or narrow its `paths:` until it stops matching, and this file
# rots exactly as a cultural tolerated set did — entries intact, checker still
# correct, enforcement silently gone, nothing red to say so. lint-workflows.py's
# SR001 guards the schedule-only half; nothing guards the `paths:` half. Read the
# banner above that workflow's `on:` block before changing either.
#   a listed test not in the ledger-> UNACCOUNTED, the job fails. A tolerated
#                                     test that silently stopped being RUN is
#                                     how the list rots into fiction.
# This file could not be written before 2026-08-06: #737 established that
# tests-slow-integration.yml had never once executed (schedule-only, and the
# file never reached the default branch, so GitHub 404s the workflow), so no
# ledger existed to enumerate FROM. Pinning a tolerated set requires having
# measured one — the first entry came from the first SLOW-band ledger ever
# produced, run locally on 2026-08-06.
# Format: <test-path><TAB><issue-ref><TAB><one-line reason>
# Adding a line REQUIRES an issue ref: an entry with nobody's name on it is how
# a toleration outlives the reason for it.
# THE SET IS CURRENTLY EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE INTENDED RESTING STATE — not a
# disabled check. An empty tolerated set means every SLOW scenario is expected
# to PASS, so slow-band-drift.sh's NEW-RED arm covers the whole band with
# nothing exempted. Do not read the absence of entries as "nothing is being
# checked"; read it as "nothing is being excused".
# The one entry this file ever held, and why it is gone:
#   monitor/watcher/test-respawn-loop-integration.sh — tolerated
#   2026-08-06 under your-org/nexus-code#738 for the product bug
#   your-org/nexus-code#741 (`_target_window_present` decided presence by
#   WINDOW NAME ALONE, so a `remain-on-exit` corpse read as PRESENT and the
#   absent branch never fired a second time: 1 respawn, 1 stub crash, guard
#   needs 3). #741 is FIXED — the probe now reads `#{pane_dead}`, and
#   `_respawn_verify_target_absent` no longer mistakes a corpse for an
#   unclassifiable occupant — so the toleration became exactly the
#   STALE-TOLERATION this file's second direction exists to reject, and it
#   cost the deletion it was designed to cost.
#   The entry recorded one deliberately OPEN question: why the test ever
#   passed LOCALLY, with a prior race hypothesis marked refuted. That question
#   is now CLOSED, measured rather than argued. The corpse forms if and only if
#   `remain-on-exit` is in effect at the instant the spawned child exits, and
#   `_respawn_spawn_window` sets the option AFTER `new-window`. Four arms, 12
#   trials each, deterministic in every arm: fast pane + instant-exit child ->
#   VANISHED 12/12; the same with the option preset -> corpse 12/12; the same
#   with a child that sleeps 1s -> corpse 12/12; a slow pane (login-shell rc
#   chain) + instant-exit child -> corpse 12/12. The earlier refutation ran its
#   control only in the arm where the option always wins, which is why it
#   measured 12/12 PERSISTED and concluded there was no race. The historical
#   green was then reproduced directly: re-creating the pre-#737 fixture drift
#   (dropping the `monitor/_*.sh` copy line) makes the spawned launcher die
#   instantly, it loses the race, no corpse forms, and the crash-loop guard
#   TRIPS — the test passed while never once running the stub, which is the
#   very thing its crash-log assertion was later added to catch. In production
#   the margin is not close: the launcher execs claude, which outlives
#   `set-window-option` by orders of magnitude, so the corpse always forms.
